title: Etale descent of one singular-point blowup on a nodal trait curve
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ be flat and finitely presented [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose every nonempty geometric fibre is reduced of pure dimension one and every nonsmooth closed geometric point has completed local ring $\Omega[[a,b]]/(ab)$, where $\Omega$ is the algebraically closed geometric ground field [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. No connectedness or nonemptiness of the geometric fibres is assumed. Fix a closed nonregular point $x\in X_k$ and a diagram of etale $S$-maps $(X,x)\leftarrow(U,u)\to(M_n,o)$ with $n\geq2$, where $R\to R'$ is a local injective etale extension of DVRs, $\pi$ is a uniformizer of $R'$, $M_n=\operatorname{Spec}(R'[a,b]/(ab-\pi^n))$, and $o=(\pi,a,b)$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $b:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_xX\to X$ be the ordinary blowup of the reduced point [def-nagata-global-blowup]. After restricting $U$ to an open neighbourhood of $u$, the scheme-theoretic inverse images of both reduced points $x$ and $o$ are exactly the reduced point $u$. The two comparison squares obtained by blowing up $u$, $x$ and $o$ are Cartesian, their top maps are etale, and $\operatorname{Bl}_uU\to X^+$ covers every point above $x$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The morphism $X^+\to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation with every nonempty geometric fibre reduced, pure-one-dimensional and nodal; here nodal means the same completed-local-ring condition just stated. Its generic fibre is isomorphic to $X_K$, and $b$ is an isomorphism over $X\setminus\{x\}$. If $n=2$ or $3$, all points above $x$ are regular. If $n\geq4$, exactly one point $x^+$ above $x$ is nonregular, it is closed in $X^+$, and it admits a common pointed etale neighbourhood with the origin of $\operatorname{Spec}(R'[r,s]/(rs-\pi^{n-2}))$. There are no new nonregular points away from $x$. No excellence, completeness, perfection or characteristic restriction is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CDE (lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal), second and last paragraphs, with Tag 0CDC (example-blowup), and Divisors Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up). The stopping cases are n=2 and n=3.

proof.text: Write $p:U\to X$, $q:U\to M_n$ and $L=\kappa(u)$. The etale-fibre theorem says that each fibre over a point is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of its residue field. In particular $u$ is open in both reduced fibres $p^{-1}(x)$ and $q^{-1}(o)$. Choose an open neighbourhood of $u$ inducing just that singleton in each fibre, and intersect the two neighbourhoods. Since the fibres are reduced, both scheme-theoretic inverse images are now $\operatorname{Spec}L$, with their original embeddings into $U$. Thus their ideal sheaves coincide with the ideal of the reduced closed point $u$. The restricted maps remain etale by the open-immersion and composition clauses. Also $L/\kappa(x)$ and $L/\kappa(o)$ are finite separable; no equality of these fields is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0CDE (lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal), second paragraph: shrink U and identify reduced centres; morphisms.tex Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field).

proof.text:
Put $B=\operatorname{Bl}_oM_n$ and $U^+=\operatorname{Bl}_uU$. Etale maps are flat by their definition. Apply the flat blowup comparison to $p$ and $q$, with the inverse-image centres just identified. The comparison theorem gives
$$U^+\cong U\times_X X^+\cong U\times_{M_n}B$$
over the indicated bases, so both squares are Cartesian. The two top arrows $p^+:U^+\to X^+$ and $q^+:U^+\to B$ are etale by stability under base change. Associating these fibre products gives
$$U^+_u\cong X^+_x\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)}\operatorname{Spec}L
\cong B_o\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(o)}\operatorname{Spec}L.$$
The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is surjective, since both spaces have one point. Its base change $U^+_u\to X^+_x$ is surjective. This proves that $p^+$ covers every point above $x$, even when $\kappa(u)\ne\kappa(x)$.

source.place: Tag 0CDE, Cartesian blowup diagram; divisors.tex Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up); morphisms.tex Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective).

proof.text: The global blowup complement theorem gives $b^{-1}(X\setminus\{x\})\cong X\setminus\{x\}$. Since $x$ belongs to the special fibre, the whole generic fibre lies in this complement. Therefore $X^+_K\cong X_K$. Local rings away from $x$ are unchanged, so no new nonregular point occurs there. Together with the previous step this gives the jointly surjective etale family consisting of $p^+:U^+\to X^+$ and the open immersion $b^{-1}(X\setminus\{x\})\hookrightarrow X^+$.

source.place: Tag 0CDE, descent paragraph; divisors.tex Tag 0802 (lemma-blowing-up), isomorphism off the centre.

proof.text:
Apply the existing DVR chart calculation over $R'$. The blowup $B$ is covered by
$$\operatorname{Spec}R'[a,t]/(at-\pi),\quad
\operatorname{Spec}R'[r,s]/(rs-\pi^{n-2}),\quad
\operatorname{Spec}R'[b,h]/(bh-\pi).$$
The maps on the outer charts have $b=a^{n-1}t^n$ and $a=b^{n-1}h^n$, and on the middle chart $a=\pi r$, $b=\pi s$. These finite presentations give local finite presentation. The chart calculation gives flatness and nodality. More explicitly every geometric chart fibre is a binomial curve $C_c$, so the field calculation gives reducedness and pure dimension one, and smoothness away from its crossing. The monomial completion calculation with two variables and ideal $(ab)$ gives exactly $\Omega[[a,b]]/(ab)$ at that crossing. Thus $B\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ has the fibre condition required here, including purity. Both outer charts are regular. For $n=2$ the middle chart has $rs=1$ and is smooth; for $n=3$ it is the regular model $rs=\pi$; for $n\ge4$ its only nonregular point is $w^+=(\pi,r,s)$, by the regularity criterion for $M_{n-2}$. Its residue field is $\kappa(o)$, as is immediate from the displayed coordinates.

source.place: Tag 0CDC (example-blowup), three affine charts; the n=3 regular stopping case follows from the same example at exponent one.

proof.text: Use the scheme case of nodal chart locality for the diagram $B\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ over $B\to S$, whose left vertical arrow is the identity and whose right vertical arrow is the given etale map. Its existential-chart criterion applies because the identity is surjective. Hence $B\to S$ is nodal of relative dimension one. Nodal source locality then gives $U^+\to S$ nodal: to obtain preservation under the possibly nonsurjective $q^+$, apply that locality equivalence to the jointly surjective family $\{\mathrm{id}_B,q^+\}$ on $B$. The complement from step 3 has the original nodal fibre condition, by restriction of $f$. Applying source locality once more to the two-member covering of $X^+$ in step 3 proves that $X^+\to S$ is flat, locally of finite presentation, and has pure-one-dimensional geometric fibres with the specified completed local rings at nonsmooth points. These locality statements explicitly allow empty fibres and impose no connectedness requirement.

source.place: Tag 0CDE, nodality descent paragraph; curves.tex Tags 0CD8 (lemma-nodal-family-postcompose-etale) and 0C5D (lemma-nodal-family-etale-local-source); spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0DSG (lemma-nodal-local), scheme specialization.

proof.text: Check reducedness explicitly as well. For a geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, the etale fibre theorem identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(R'\otimes_R\Omega)$ with a disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: its residue extensions are finite separable and $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. Consequently $B_\Omega$ has an open cover by the reduced binomial curves of step 4. Etale base change and the theorem that an etale scheme over a reduced scheme is reduced give reducedness of $U^+_\Omega$. The other member of the geometric covering is reduced by the hypothesis on $X$. These two morphisms still cover: above $x$ this follows from the fibre formula in step 2 and stability of surjectivity under base change; elsewhere the open member covers. At any point of $X^+_\Omega$ choose a point of this covering. The map of local rings $A\to D$ is faithfully flat by etale stalk invariance and $D$ is reduced. It is injective: if $aD=0$, flatness gives $(aA)\otimes_A D=0$, and faithfulness gives $aA=0$. Thus any nilpotent of $A$ is zero. All geometric fibres of $X^+\to S$ are therefore reduced.

source.place: Tag 0CDE, descent of the fibre condition; morphisms.tex Tags 02GL and 02GO; etale.tex Tag 025O (proposition-etale-reduced).

proof.text:
Etale stalk invariance compares regularity at each point of $U^+$ with regularity at its images under both $p^+$ and $q^+$. If $n=2$ or $3$, all of $B$ is regular by step 4, so every point above $x$ is regular, since it lifts to $U^+_u$. If $n\ge4$, any nonregular point of $U^+_u$ must map to $w^+$. The second fibre identification in step 2 shows that its full inverse image in $U^+_u$ is
$$\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\kappa(w^+)\otimes_{\kappa(o)}L\bigr)=\operatorname{Spec}L,$$
since $\kappa(w^+)=\kappa(o)$. Thus there is exactly one such point $u^+$, and it is nonregular by the same etale stalk criterion. Its image $x^+=p^+(u^+)$ is nonregular. Every nonregular point above $x$ lifts to this same $u^+$, proving uniqueness. Notice that uniqueness uses the rationality of $w^+$ over $o$ and the Cartesian fibre formula; it does not follow merely from an arbitrary etale image containing one singular point.

source.place: Tag 0CDE, last paragraph, residue-field argument for the unique residual singularity, applied only for n>=4; more-algebra.tex Tag 0AH0 (lemma-regular-etale-extension).

proof.text: For $n\ge4$ restrict $U^+$ to the inverse image under $q^+$ of the middle chart in step 4. It contains $u^+$ and has etale maps to $X^+$ and to $\operatorname{Spec}(R'[r,s]/(rs-\pi^{n-2}))$, sending $u^+$ to $x^+$ and the origin. This is the required common pointed etale neighbourhood. Finally $x^+$ is closed, not just relatively isolated. A finite-presentation affine chart of $f$ through $x$, reduced modulo $\pi$, is a finite-type $k$-scheme in which $x$ is closed. The closed-point field criterion therefore gives $\kappa(x)/k$ finite. Step 1 gives $L/\kappa(x)$ finite, and step 7 gives $\kappa(u^+)=L$. The residue-field embedding $\kappa(x^+)\hookrightarrow L$ consequently makes $\kappa(x^+)/k$ finite. Since $X^+\to S$ is locally of finite presentation by step 5, it is locally of finite type (the local algebra presentations have finitely many generators). The finite-residue-point theorem makes $x^+$ closed in the special fibre, which is closed in $X^+$, hence closed in $X^+$. All inputs used apply to arbitrary DVRs and arbitrary residue characteristic.

No new nodes. Source: I read Stacks models.tex 0CDC and 0CDE in full; the 8 steps follow 0CDE's second and last paragraphs. Confirmed source error: 0CDE says that for n>2 there is a unique singular point, but for n=3 the middle chart rs=π is M_1 and regular. The item already handles this (n=2,3 regular; n>=4 has one residual point, exponent n-2), which matches what the parent regularization step 2 uses. Steps: (1) the étale-fibre node isolates u in both fibres, so the scheme-theoretic inverse images are the reduced point u. (2) For flat maps, J=I·O_U is the ideal of the inverse image, so the flat blowup comparison gives Cartesian squares; the top maps are étale by base change; U+_u = X+_x ×_κ(x) Spec L, and surjective base change gives coverage even when L≠κ(x). (3) The complement theorem gives X+_K ≅ X_K. (4) The DVR chart node applies over R' with π as uniformizer. Nodality is derived explicitly from binomial-fibres plus monomial-completion (r=2, α=(1,1)), which avoids the connectedness that def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres imports. Regularity: outer charts are M_1, rs=1 is smooth, n=3 gives M_1, n>=4 gives M_{n-2}; κ(w+)=κ(o). (5) Space-chart locality with (id_B, Spec R'→S) gives B→S nodal; source locality on {id_B,q+} and then on {p+, complement} gives X+→S nodal. The closed versus all nonsmooth points difference is harmless, since generic points of a reduced curve over Ω are smooth. (6) Reducedness descends by faithfully flat injectivity, written out correctly. (7) The preimage of w+ is Spec(κ(w+)⊗L) = Spec L, one point; uniqueness follows by surjectivity. (8) The middle-chart preimage is the common neighbourhood; κ(x)/k is finite by Zariski on an affine chart of X_k, κ(x+) ⊂ L is finite, so 01TE makes x+ closed in X+_s, which is closed. Edge cases checked: n=2, 3, 4; κ(u)≠κ(x); imperfect k; characteristic 2. Duplicate search (0CDE, rg -L) finds only the parent and its Q56 siblings; none states the item. The declared tool_uses are all generic and accepted; no SGA.
